last_assistant_message:
All three confirmed-bad records are gone (`EXE32D` was untracked so it just vanishes cleanly; `SYJXKR`/`SDJRUV` show as tracked deletions since they'd been committed in an earlier session). `YWMW6Z` untouched throughout.

**[Rigby]: Found three distinct, compounding bugs — not just one. Fixed all three, verified each in isolation, zero regressions.**

**Bug 1 — `detect_workflow()`'s run-verb-adjacency check fired on later, unrelated clauses of a longer message.** My 11-case suite only tested short prompts; it never covered a long dispatch/discussion message where a workflow name and an unrelated run-verb both happen to appear, just in different clauses. Fixed by restricting all non-path/non-slash matching to the prompt's **first clause only** (split on sentence-enders) — exactly the fix direction you suggested. I could not recover the literal historical prompt text for SYJXKR/SDJRUV/EXE32D (the hook never logged prompt text — see below), so I reconstructed the failure *class* from your timing account and verified against that directly. Added 5 new real-incident-shaped cases to a permanent 26-case regression suite now saved at `.claude/hooks/tests/test_detect_workflow.py` — all pass, no regressions on the prior 21.

**Bug 2 — stale state.yaml completion falsely finalized fresh spurious records as instant "success."** Checked the live data: `workflows/shutdown-cleanup/state.yaml` has sat at `status: complete` since **2026-08-12** — 15 days stale. `eval-turn-stop.py` only checked "is status currently terminal," never *when* it became terminal, so a spurious record opened weeks later closed as a fake "success" in 26.8s off nothing but leftover state. This is a second, independent bug from #1 — it explains SDJRUV (5.02s) and EXE32D (11.09s) closing so fast with 0 subagents, regardless of what triggered them. Fixed: `try_finalize()` now requires state.yaml's own completion timestamp to be at/after the eval record's own `started` time. Added a bounded 2-hour stale-abort path so a genuinely spurious record doesn't sit open forever. Verified all three branches (stale→stays open, stale-and-old→aborts, genuinely-fresh→succeeds) in a sandboxed reproduction of the exact CKQQD4 shape.

**Bug 3 — subagent misattribution.** SYJXKR's linked subagent `ac40f2ffdbe8a2390` was mine (capability-build work), not a real boot subagent. Root cause: the linking logic picked "the most recent open turn-level record for this session_id" with no check for whether it was the *only* candidate. Fixed with `find_unambiguous_open_turn_record()` — skips linking entirely when more than one turn-level record is open for the session, rather than guessing. Verified: 1 open record links, 2+ refuses.

**Also added, since I couldn't diagnose the original incident from logs at all:** `trigger_evidence` (truncated matched-clause text, capped at 200 chars) now gets written into every opened record, and `TURN-START` log lines include it too. This is fixed going forward only — I want to be upfront that I did not literally recover what text opened SYJXKR/SDJRUV/EXE32D; I inferred the failure class from your account and the code path, and closed that class, not that specific transcript.

Also noticed (not part of this ask, not touched): more real concurrent activity landed again — a Scott McMichael 1:1 note/person file, morning-briefing and one-on-one-prep state changes, new error entries. Left alone.

`evolutions/.pending-changes.json` updated under the same `work-20260826-193329-eval-hook-lifecycle` item. All hook files compile; `settings.json` untouched this round.
